newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CAP figures removed from cohesion report.
newsitem.headline: CAP figures removed from cohesion report.

text.p: A European Commission report on cohesion policy may have been edited to remove statistics showing that major food exporting countries gained more from the Common Agricultural Policy than importers, agriculture policy analyst Brian Gardner said on Thursday.

"The version of the 'First Cohesion Report' finally published by the European Commission on Wednesday has clearly been quite significantly altered to avoid giving offence to certain member states' governments' sensitivity on gains and losses accruing from the operation of the EC's Common Agricultural Policy," he told Reuters.
An earlier draft obtained by Reuters contained additional statistics.

According to Gardner the original had shown that countries with large food export industries were major beneficiaries of the CAP, while those such as Portugal, in a net food importing position and which produced products attracting few European Union subsidies, were paying more to the CAP budget than they received.

A prominent feature of the draft version circulated to some journalists in Brussels was a table detailing the gains and losses to the agriculture industries and their national economies resulting from operation of the CAP.
"These are figures which the Commission's Agricultural Directorate (DGVI) has always been loath to allow into the public domains," Gardner said.
He added that the missing statistics showed that the CAP had done nothing to alleviate poverty in the disadvantaged rural regions of the Community.
The original version also indicated that the 1992 CAP reforms have done little to right the in-built bias of the CAP towards the agriculturally efficient and relatively wealthy, he said.

Commission sources said on Friday that in the inter- departmental consultations prior to publication, DGVI officials insisted that the report -- prepared by the Regional Directorate of Commissioner Monika Wolf Mathies -- should not contain the critical passages.
The spokesman for Commissioner Mathies could not be contacted immediately for comment.
